report_deadline.quote:
(c) The Commission shall submit its final report and recommenda­
tions to the Committee no later than eighteen months after the date 
of its first meeting,' and may make any interim reports which it deems 
would expedite the work of the Committee.

termination_trigger.quote:
S ec. 6. Term ination o f the Committee and the Commission.  The 
Committee and the Commission shall terminate ninety days after the 
submission of the final report of the Commission.

executed_revocations.quote:
S ec. 7. Revocation o f orders. Executive Order 10472 of July 20, 
1953, and Executive Order 10937 of May 3, 1961, are hereby revoked.

compensation.quote:
(d) Each member of the Commission may be compensated for each 
day such member is engaged upon the work of the Commission, and 
shall be reimbursed for travel expenses, including per diem in lieu of 
subsistence, as authorized by law (5 U.S.C. 55a; 5 U.S.C. 73b-2) for 
persons in the Government service employed intermittently.

gsa_reimbursement.quote:
(c) The General Services Administration is hereby designated as 
the agency which shall, on a reimbursable basis, provide administrative 
services for the Commission.

formal_revocation.quote:
Sec. 18. Executive Order No. 11256, establishing the President’s Committee on  
Food and Fiber and establishing the National Advisory Commission on Food  
and Fiber, is revoked.

independent_findings: The original has twenty substantive units when the section 2(a) and 4(b) lead-ins are joined to their enumerated duties: sections 1(a)-(b), 2(a)(1)-(2) and 2(b), 3(a)-(e), 4(a), 4(b)(1)-(3), 4(c), 5(a)-(c), 6 and 7. The page break within section 4(b) must not cause its duties to be lost.

Section 6 ends both the Committee and Commission ninety days after actual submission of the Commission final report. Section 4(c) requires a report no later than eighteen months after the first meeting; neither that deadline nor a hypothetical first-meeting date proves submission. Section 2(b) separately calls for transmission to the President with Committee recommendations. Evidence must distinguish submission to the Committee from later presidential transmission or publication.

No actual final report, submission cover letter, first-meeting record or date was located in the bounded local inventory/name scan. No earliest end date can be calculated from the held original and cleanup actor alone. This is a source gap, not exhaustion.

EO12379 section 18 expressly revokes EO11256. Its full two-page extract has no delayed effective provision or target-specific savings. August 17, 1982 supports formal revocation only and cannot displace the earlier actual-report-plus-ninety-days condition.

Section 3(d) authorizes compensation and requires travel reimbursement; section 5(c) provides reimbursable GSA services. Accrued claims and expenditures are distinct from the existence of the bodies and require residual analysis.

Section 7 directly revokes EO10472 and EO10937. Their held originals show a prior National Agricultural Advisory Commission and a membership amendment. The later expiration/revocation of EO11256 does not by its own text restore that predecessor. Exact first-end classification of the executed legal changes cannot be supplied by automatic completion or by the 1982 cleanup date.

All four issue-PDF hashes have matching official-fixity rows, but their expected PDF cache files are absent. The corpus inventory has no matching original issue/hash PDF. Full extracts read is not a page-image inspection.

Later-events EDGES.csv has only EO12379 as an acting lead on EO11256. The dossier chain falsely binds the same 1982 actor text to ten earlier actor identities/signing dates; those bindings do not establish actual earlier revocations.
